text: Grief counselling for about six months. It helped me accept that I couldn't have known. I eventually told my mother the truth, and she said she'd guessed and wasn't angry, which lifted a huge weight. Still avoid lakes.
Ich bin langsam wieder Fahrrad gefahren, erst auf leeren Wegen. Ein paar Gespräche mit einer Beratungsstelle haben geholfen.

My husband took me to my GP after the pneumonia, and I finally told her everything. She referred me to a psychiatrist, who prescribed an antidepressant and arranged weekly appointments because of the pull towards death. That was the right decision. I then started grief therapy with a therapist experienced in traumatic loss, and we've been working on separating my son from the image on the mountain. It's slow.

I joined a bereaved parents' group. Being with other parents who have lost children has been the most helpful thing. They understand the longing.

I wrote to the facilitators about what happened. They replied that every journey is perfect as it is. That hurt.

I walk every day, in daylight, on flat paths. My husband walks with me.

The pull has weakened, but I still have very dark days.

I saw a sleep specialist, who helped me with sleep restriction therapy, which worked eventually. My GP gave me a short course of sleeping pills. I tried an HPPD forum, which scared me. I now test everything with reagent kits, not that I take much anymore.
Spent a lot of time outside, hiking and climbing, to feel real. Talked to a counsellor twice. It wore off.

Ich habe einen Anwalt eingeschaltet, was mir zumindest in Bezug auf das Verfahren Sicherheit gegeben hat. Psychologisch habe ich etwa ein Jahr lang eine Verhaltenstherapie gemacht, in der es um die Angst vor der Polizei und die Albträume ging. Das hat geholfen. Ich bin auch viel in der Natur gewesen und habe mit Klettern angefangen. Mit zwei anderen Teilnehmerinnen der Zeremonie habe ich mich ein paar Mal getroffen, das war hilfreich, weil wir das Gleiche erlebt hatten.

I told the organisers how harmful their response was. They said it's very rare for someone to want to leave and that they were following protocol.

I found a trauma therapist who works with somatic approaches. We started with a lot of grounding work, very slowly. She helped me build a sense of safety in my body before we touched the memories of the hut. Later we did some EMDR on the hour by the hatch. That was very helpful.

My psychiatrist prescribed a low dose of mirtazapine for sleep, which helped. I also gradually dimmed my night light over many months, with my therapist's guidance. I can now sleep with a small light in the hallway.

My partner was very patient. We started evening walks at dusk together, which helped me approach darkness slowly.

I tried guided meditation, eyes closed, too early, and it triggered a panic attack. I now meditate with eyes open.

I'm much better, but darkness remains difficult.
Ich habe eine Weile eine Therapie gemacht, die sich auch um mein Körperbild drehte. Das hat geholfen. Spiegel sind inzwischen wieder in Ordnung.
Three follow-up sessions with the same therapist. Writing to my mother.
